contentSections: Mild steel, often called MS, is strong, easy to fabricate and cheaper than many other metals. That is why it appears in so many gates, screens, canopies and facade frames across India. But mild steel has one big weakness: it rusts. Whether an MS facade lasts 5 years or 25 depends almost entirely on how it is coated and detailed.
This guide explains how to protect mild steel, what to specify, where it makes sense and where another metal is the smarter choice.
What Is an MS or Iron Facade?

An MS facade uses mild steel sheets, plates, tubes or sections as cladding, screens, fins or structural frames. People often say iron facade or iron cladding, but the actual material is usually mild steel, which is a low carbon steel.
Typical uses include:

• Laser cut decorative screens and jaali panels
  • Fins, louvers and brise soleil
  • Gates, grills and compound walls
  • Canopies and entrance frames
  • Sub-frames behind other cladding materials
Why Mild Steel Is Popular

• Low material cost compared with stainless steel, brass or many aluminium systems
  • High strength that allows slim sections and long spans
  • Easy to cut, bend and weld, so custom shapes are simple
  • Widely available across India
  • Good for heavy duty and security uses
Why Mild Steel Rusts
Steel rusts when iron meets oxygen and moisture. Once rust starts, it spreads under paint, lifts the coating and eats into the metal. In India, several things speed this up:

• Monsoon humidity and long wet periods
  • Coastal salt in the air
  • Industrial pollution and acid rain
  • Water trapped in joints, hollow sections and corners
  • Damaged coatings from scratches, drilling or welding on site
Most early rusting does not start on flat surfaces. It starts at edges, welds, holes and joints where the coating is thin or damaged.
The Coating System: Your Real Protection
Good protection comes in layers. A typical outdoor system includes:

• Surface preparation. Remove mill scale, oil and rust, usually by shot blasting or chemical treatment. A poor start ruins every layer that follows.
  • Zinc layer. Hot dip galvanising or zinc rich primer gives sacrificial protection, so zinc corrodes before the steel does.
  • Primer. Bonds the system and adds a barrier layer.
  • Topcoat. Polyurethane paint, polyester powder coat or similar. It gives colour and UV protection.
The more severe the environment, the more important each layer becomes. Coastal and industrial sites need higher specifications than inland, dry locations.
Coating Options Compared

OptionProtection levelLookWatch out for

Zinc rich primer plus paintMediumWide colour rangeDepends on surface prep and coating thickness
Hot dip galvanising plus powder coatHighWide colour rangePanel size limited by the zinc bath, distortion on thin sheet
Galvanised onlyHighDull grey, spangledLook may not suit premium facades

For premium facades in India, hot dip galvanising followed by powder coating or a high quality paint system is usually the better specification.
Details That Prevent Rust
Coating alone is not enough. Good detailing matters just as much:

• Seal hollow sections. Open ends let water in and rust the steel from inside.
  • Add drain holes where water can collect.
  • Round or ease sharp edges. Coatings are thin on sharp corners.
  • Avoid horizontal ledges where water and dust sit.
  • Use continuous welds instead of spot welds that trap moisture.
  • Touch up site damage. Re-coat any cut, drilled or welded area before the panel is fixed.
  • Use compatible fasteners. Stainless or galvanised fasteners prevent corrosion around bolts.
  • Separate dissimilar metals with isolating washers or tapes.
Thickness Guide

Thin sheet can ripple, drum in rain and corrode through faster. Thickness depends on panel size, wind load and support spacing, so ask your engineer to confirm. Folded edges, returns and stiffeners help thin sheet stay flat without needing excessive thickness.
For laser cut screens, remember that cut edges are bare steel. They need proper coating coverage, particularly in fine patterns where gaps are small and coating can bridge or miss.
Real Costs: Looking Beyond the Price Per Kilo
Mild steel is cheap to buy, but a fair comparison includes the full life cost:

• Material and fabrication
  • Surface preparation and coating system
  • Transport and handling, since steel is heavy
  • Installation and structural support
  • Repainting and repairs over the life of the building
  • Replacement if rust damage becomes serious

A basic painted MS screen can cost less on day one but more over 10 to 15 years, once repainting and repair are counted. A well specified galvanised and powder coated system costs more at the start and usually costs less over the full life. Ask your supplier to quote both options so you can compare. MS vs Aluminium vs Stainless Steel

FactorMild steelAluminiumStainless steel
Upfront costLowestMediumHighest
WeightHeavyLightHeavy
Corrosion resistanceNeeds full coating systemNaturally highVery high
UpkeepMedium to highLowLow
Best forFrames, gates, heavy duty screens, tight budgetsMost facade cladding and screensCoastal sites, premium details

For large facade areas, aluminium often wins on total cost because it is lighter, needs less support steel and has low upkeep. Mild steel is a good choice for structural sub-frames, gates and heavy duty uses.
Upkeep Checklist

• Wash dust and salt off every few months, more often near the coast.
  • Inspect edges, welds and fixings once or twice a year.
  • Touch up chips and scratches immediately, before rust spreads.
  • Clear drain holes and gutters.
  • Plan a recoating schedule suited to your site and coating system, using our metal facade maintenance guide.
Common Mistakes

• Specifying paint only on an exposed coastal facade
  • Ignoring hollow sections and edges
  • Welding or drilling on site without touching up
  • Comparing quotes with different coating systems as if they were equal
  • Using mild steel where aluminium would be lighter and easier to maintain
